previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain, nausea, vomiting, and hypertensive emergency. Initial evaluation ruled out acute coronary syndrome and pulmonary embolism, though EKG showed ST depressions and troponin was mildly elevated, consistent with her baseline due to ESRD. Blood pressure was controlled with IV nicardipine initially, then transitioned back to oral medications. She reported odynophagia, prompting GI and ENT consultation. Laryngoscopy suggested GERD, and EGD confirmed reflux esophagitis. She was started on high-dose pantoprazole, after which symptoms resolved. Leukocytosis, likely related to esophageal inflammation, improved without antibiotics. She remained stable throughout the stay, with controlled diabetes, continued dialysis, and no seizure activity. She was discharged to an extended care facility on pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily for eight weeks, with follow-up arranged with PCP and GI.

#SOFT TISSUE INFECTION
She was admitted with a leukocytosis to 14 in the context of 
increased lethargy and decreased appetite.  She had multiple

to under her left breast, under her pannus on the left, and her 
right thigh.  She was started ___ on vancomycin and zosyn,

stabilized at ~12.7.  She remained afebrile throughout. Despite

cause pain and was becoming more purulent. A CT of the R leg

wounds and her wounds continued to expand.  Unfortunately, she 
started having brief episodes of hypotension and altered mental

up-titration of 3 vasopressors. A goals of care discussion was 
revisited with family and it was agreed that patient would be 
DNR/DNI but vasopressors could be continued. Patient was given 
IV dilaudid to ensure comfort from pain. She passed comfortably 
with her daughters at her bedside. She was pronounced dead on 
___ on ___
